questions.correction: The source answer is questionable because the stem explicitly states there is no evidence of cervical spine injury; in an unconscious trauma patient, airway protection with endotracheal intubation is generally the definitive airway intervention when indicated. Jaw thrust is primarily emphasized when cervical spine injury is suspected.
questions.correctedQuestion: A trauma patient is unconscious with no evidence of cervical spine injury. The best initial definitive airway management is:
questions.explanation: In an unconscious trauma patient, airway protection and definitive airway management are prioritized. If there is no cervical spine injury concern, endotracheal intubation is generally preferred when a definitive airway is required.

optionExplanations.A: Cricothyrotomy is not the best answer for the question as written.
optionExplanations.B: Jaw thrust is not the best answer for the question as written.
optionExplanations.C: Jaw thrust is preferred when cervical spine injury is a concern because it minimizes neck movement; however, the stem states no cervical injury.
optionExplanations.D: Tracheostomy is not the best answer for the question as written.

questions.subject: Neonatology
questions.title: Initial delivery-room care
questions.originalQuestion: The first management of a newborn in the delivery room is:

originalOptions.C: Clear the airway by suctioning the mouth and nose if needed

sourceAnswer.text: C — Clear the airway by suctioning the mouth and nose if needed

questions.correction: The source answer is questionable because routine suctioning of the mouth and nose is not recommended for a vigorous newborn. Initial care is drying, warming, positioning and assessment; suction is performed only when obstruction is present or ventilation requires it.
questions.correctedQuestion: The initial management of a vigorous newborn in the delivery room is:

correctAnswer.text: No valid single answer based on current evidence; the stem requires revision.

questions.explanation: Routine newborn care begins with drying, warming, positioning and assessment of breathing and heart rate. Suctioning is not routinely performed unless the airway is obstructed.

optionExplanations.A: Oxygen therapy is not the best answer for the question as written.
optionExplanations.B: Remove vernix is not the best answer for the question as written.
optionExplanations.C: Clear the airway by suctioning the mouth and nose if needed is not the best answer for the question as written.
optionExplanations.D: Immediate feeding is not the best answer for the question as written.
